request.user:
Subject: Physics
Question type: single-correct (exactly one option is right)

A block of weight 100 N when pushed by a force F on a horizontal rough surface moves with an acceleration 1 m / s^2 , when force is doubled its acceleration becomes 10 m / s^2 . The coefficient of friction between block and surface is ( g = 10 m / s^2 )
(A) 0.8
(B) 0.4
(C) 0.6
(D) 0.2

result.working:
Weight 100 N, so m = 100/10 = 10 kg. Taking F as horizontal, kinetic friction = 100μ.
Case 1: F − 100μ = 10 × 1 = 10.
Case 2: 2F − 100μ = 10 × 10 = 100.
Subtracting case 1 from case 2 gives F = 90 N.
Then 90 − 100μ = 10, so μ = 0.8.
result.note: The question does not state the direction of F. It is taken as horizontal, the standard reading.
